title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page sets up an integral (or arbitrary-coefficient) divided-power de Rham theory for simplicial sets. It works inside the topos of simplicial sets.

(1) Setup. The ambient topos is Ss = Δ^ (presheaves on Δ), and k is a commutative ring. Grothendieck sets L_* = L_{*k} = i_{0*}(k) = L_Z ⊗_Z k. Here i_0* is the right adjoint of X ↦ X_0, i.e. the 0-coskeleton, so L_n = k^{[n]} = k^{n+1}. Concretely, L is the presheaf of k-valued functions on the vertices of Δ^n, i.e. the linear coordinate functions t_0,…,t_n. L is taken as a sheaf of k-modules, not of rings. It carries the global section T = (1,…,1) = t_0+…+t_n, which gives an injection k_* → L_*.

(2) The bigraded algebra C. Let C^{**}_* = Γ^*_k L ⊗_k Λ^* L. This is a bigraded differential algebra with divided powers, with differential of bidegree (−1,+1): d(x^{[p]}) = x^{[p−1]} dx. It is alternating for the total degree. In a margin note, the notation L̄ stands for Λ^1 L, and x̄ for the element of L̄ corresponding to x in L.

C is a resolution of k: C^{00} = k_*, and for total degree n > 0 the PD-Koszul / PD-Poincaré complex 0 → Γ^n L → Γ^{n−1}L⊗Λ^1L → … → Λ^n L → 0 is exact. All its terms are flasque, being built from the coskeletal sheaf L.

(3) Defining DR as a kernel. Set T̄ = dT ∈ Γ(Ss, C^{01}) ≅ Γ(Ss, L̄). Multiplication T̄∧ : C → C has bidegree (0,1) and square zero. It anticommutes with d, since d(T̄x) = dT̄·x − T̄dx = −T̄dx because dT̄ = 0. It is injective on C^{*0}, and Im = Ker because T̄ is unimodular (Koszul exactness).

Grothendieck defines DR^{pq} = Ker(T̄∧ : C^{p,q+1} → C^{p,q+2}) ≅ Γ^p L ⊗ Ker(Λ^{q+1}L → Λ^{q+2}L) ≅ Γ^p L ⊗ Λ^q Ψ, where Ψ = L/k·T. DR^{**} gets the bigrading and differential induced from C, up to sign and a shift by one in total degree. It also gets a PD-multiplicative structure, characterized on the next page by requiring u = T̄∧ : C → DR to be compatible with all structures.

(4) What DR is concretely. Evaluated on Δ^n, DR^{p,q} consists of homogeneous divided-power polynomials of degree p in t_0,…,t_n times q-forms in the dt_i modulo Σdt_i = 0. This is a homogenized ('weighted') PD version of Sullivan/Cartan polynomial forms on simplices. The relation Σt_i = 1 is not imposed; it is replaced by the auxiliary weight grading and the operator T̄∧.

(5) Where it leads. The next page applies Hom(X_*, −) and gets a bigraded PD dga C(X) with axioms (A) and (B). It shows H^n(C^{0,*}, T̄∧) ≅ H^{n−1}(X,k) for n ≥ 2. So the purpose is a functorial, strictly (PD-)commutative cochain-level model computing H^*(X;k) for any ring k, including Z and F_p. This is the 'complexe de De Rham à puissances divisées' of the 1976 IHÉS lecture.
errors: No substantive error. Minor point: T itself lies in Γ^1L = C^{1,0} (as the next page says), while T̄ = dT lies in C^{0,1}. The phrase 'Γ(Ss, C^{10})' on the page is consistent with this.
The identification Ker(Λ^{q+1}L → Λ^{q+2}L) ≅ Λ^q(L/kT) uses that T̄ is a unimodular (split) section; this holds since k → L is split degreewise. Grothendieck leaves this implicit.
The signs and degree shift of the induced differential on DR are left as 'au signe près'. They are not fully specified on this page.

ideas.what: Use the 0-coskeleton sheaf L = cosk_0(k) (coordinate functions on simplices) and its symmetric/divided-power and exterior algebras as flasque sheaves on Δ^ to build cochain models.
ideas.modern_name: Polynomial (PL) de Rham forms on simplices as a simplicial cdga
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977), H. Cartan (Théories cohomologiques, 1976), Bousfield–Gugenheim (1976) over Q

ideas.what: Replace polynomials by divided powers, so the Poincaré lemma (exactness of the Γ⊗Λ Koszul complex) holds over any ring k, including Z.
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power de Rham complex / PD Poincaré lemma (crystalline-style) applied to simplices
ideas.usually_credited_to: PD Poincaré lemma: Berthelot/Grothendieck crystalline theory. Integral simplicial forms: Cenkl–Porter ('tame' forms, c.1981); later integral models (Mandell, Toën, Horel)
ideas.where_published: PD Poincaré lemma is in Berthelot's Cohomologie cristalline (1974); the simplicial-set application is not in published Grothendieck texts as far as known

ideas.what: Homogenized version: keep a weight grading (Γ^p) and replace the relation Σt_i = 1 by the section T and the square-zero operator T̄∧ = dT∧. DR is defined as Ker(T̄∧) ≅ Γ^p L ⊗ Λ^q(L/kT), with the PD algebra structure transported via u = T̄∧.
ideas.modern_name: Weighted/homogeneous PD forms on simplices; Koszul trick with a unimodular 1-form

ideas.what: Exactness of 0 → Γ^nL → Γ^{n−1}L⊗Λ^1L → … → Λ^nL → 0 (Koszul/de Rham complex of a divided power algebra on a free module).

missed.claim: A functorial bigraded PD-dga on simplicial sets: homogeneous divided-power polynomial forms Γ^pL⊗Λ^q(L/kT), with L = cosk_0(k), computing H^*(X;k) for arbitrary k (incl. Z). The weight grading and the operator dT∧ replace the relation Σt_i = 1. This is an integral analogue of Sullivan's PL forms. The literature usually attributes integral/p-adic cochain-model attempts to Cenkl–Porter, Karoubi, Mandell and Toën rather than to a 1976 Grothendieck construction.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and mod-p commutative cochain models are an active topic (Mandell's E∞ theorem, Toën's schematization via cosimplicial binomial rings, Horel's integral homotopy theory). A weight-graded PD-commutative model sidesteps the Steenrod-operation obstruction to strictly commutative cochains by spreading cohomology across a connecting map (H^n(C^{0,*}) ≅ H^{n−1}(X)). It may give an explicit alternative worth comparing with these works.

missed.claim: The construction links crystalline PD techniques (PD Poincaré lemma) to the problem of commutative cochain algebras for homotopy types. This anticipates later 'schematization' themes in Pursuing Stacks and Toën's work.
missed.quote: On a l'Algèbre bigraduée différentielle à p.d. … Γ^*_k L_* ⊗_k Λ L_* qui est une résolution de k
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Could connect divided-power/crystalline methods with integral rational-homotopy-type models in a way not explicitly made in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, apparently unpublished construction of a PD de Rham complex on simplicial sets with a weight-grading trick (dT∧) instead of the relation Σt_i = 1. Related ideas exist (Sullivan/Cartan forms; Cenkl–Porter integral forms; later E∞ and binomial approaches), so it is a notable unpublished variant rather than a shock. Its precise relationship to the literature is uncertain.
transcription_corrections: '(S_∞)_1 = Δ^' should read '(Ss) = Δ^' (the topos of simplicial sets); likewise 'Γ(S_∞, …)' should be 'Γ(Ss, …)'.
'h anneau commu' should be 'k anneau commutatif'; 'L_Z ⊗_Z h' should be 'L_Z ⊗_Z k'.
In 'C^{**}_{*k} = Γ^*_k L ⊗ Λ L', the first factor is the divided-power algebra Γ (the transcription's Λ^*_k is wrong).
Margin note: 'Notation L̄_* pour Λ^1 L_* et x̄ pour l'élément de L̄ correspondant à x de L' (Λ^1, not Λ̂).
The struck word before 'différentielle à p.d.' is 'anticom[mutative]', replaced by the added 'alg. alternée pour degré tot'.
'de carré nul, Im(T̄∧) = Ker(T̄∧)' is a marginal addition; '(commutant à d' is corrected to 'anticommutant à d'.
